Definition: Whether the country has enacted legal or regulatory requirements mandating that certain categories of data (personal data, government data, financial data, or critical infrastructure data) be stored within national borders. Central to data sovereignty debates in Africa.
redteam_note: Scored >0 but NO source cited — unsupported claim, verify first. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Confirmed. Lesotho's Data Protection Act (No. 5 of 2012/2013) conditions cross-border transfer of personal data (SADC-adequacy-style rules requiring consent or equivalent protection in the destination country) but does not mandate that data be stored within Lesotho, and no separate data-localisation law was found; a 2025 legal commentary confirms the regulator (Data Protection Commission) has still not even been constituted. Code 1 (no data localisation requirements) is supported and retained.

Definition: The maturity of the country's technology startup ecosystem, based on the number of tech startups, venture capital activity, accelerators/incubators, and the presence of a supportive ecosystem. Africa's startup scene is well-documented by trackers like Partech, Disrupt Africa, and Briter Bridges.
redteam_note: Scored >0 but NO source cited — unsupported claim, verify first. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Confirmed, with caveat. Dealroom's 2025/2026 country profile shows effectively zero tracked enterprise value, no unicorns and no disclosed VC rounds for Lesotho; AfriLabs' directory lists three small entrepreneurship/innovation hubs (Makhala Thekiso Foundation, BAM Group, The Hub) plus a government-run Entrepreneurship Hub & Seed Financing Facility. Hub count (3-4) is slightly higher than the '1-2' wording of code 2, but funding activity is negligible rather than the 'regular funding rounds' required for code 3 (Developing), so 2 remains the best fit on the scale.

Definition: The size and vibrancy of the local software developer and technology professional community. Measured through proxies such as GitHub activity, Stack Overflow representation, local tech meetup groups, and developer surveys. Indicates the country's capacity to build and maintain digital systems locally.
redteam_note: Scored >0 but NO source cited — unsupported claim, verify first. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: No country-specific developer count exists for Lesotho in any tracker. GitHub Octoverse's 2022 list of fastest-growing African developer communities (Nigeria, Ethiopia, Ghana, Kenya, Morocco) does not include Lesotho, and manual searches found only a handful of individual Lesotho-based developer/GitHub profiles, consistent with a very small community; LNDC (2025) describes only an 'emerging' cadre of developers. Evidence is circumstantial rather than a hard count, so code 1 is retained but the boundary with code 2 (emerging, <1,000 developers) is uncertain — flagged for human review if a firmer figure (e.g. a national ICT skills census) becomes available.

Definition: The proportion of the population with basic digital skills (ability to use a computer, smartphone, or the internet for simple tasks such as sending messages, finding information, or using apps). Based on ITU household survey data, Afrobarometer, or national ICT surveys.
redteam_note: Scored >0 but NO source cited — unsupported claim, verify first. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Changed. The Lesotho Communications Authority, with the Bureau of Statistics, ran a national ICT household survey in 2023 (ITU-manual methodology, comparative report published 2025) finding 35.1% of individuals had basic or above-basic ICT skills (19.4% basic + 15.7% above-basic). This falls in the 25-39% band (code 3), well above the unsourced code-1 (<10%) claim, so the score is revised upward to 3.
